title: GOD: Enhancing Generalization via Deep Grafting for Sequential Recommendation
abstract: arXiv:2608.16073v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Sequential recommenders often struggle with sparse and noisy histories, limiting generalization to unseen interactions. Knowledge distillation mitigates this by transferring dense supervision from a teacher to a student. However, most distillation methods run teacher and student independently, then match student outputs or representations to the teacher. Such supervision entangles student-component effects, blurring whether weak generalization stems from unreliable embeddings, overfitted encoding, or co-adaptation to sparse histories. In this paper, we propose Graft-Oriented Distillation (GOD), a component-level distillation framework for improved generalization through grafting. Grafting denotes replacing selected frozen-teacher components with trainable student counterparts to build hybrid source models. GOD uses these hybrid models to evaluate student embeddings with the teacher encoder and the student encoder with teacher embedding

translated_title: GOD：通过深度嫁接增强序列推荐泛化能力
translated_abstract: 序列推荐器常常面临历史数据稀疏和噪声的问题，这限制了对未见交互的泛化能力。知识蒸馏通过将密集监督从教师模型转移到学生模型来缓解这一问题。然而，大多数蒸馏方法独立运行教师和学生模型，然后将学生输出或表示与教师匹配。这种监督方式纠缠了学生组件的效应，模糊了弱泛化究竟源于不可靠的嵌入、过拟合的编码，还是对稀疏历史的共适应。在本文中，我们提出嫁接导向蒸馏（GOD），一种通过嫁接实现改进泛化的组件级蒸馏框架。嫁接指的是用可训练的学生组件替换选定的冻结教师组件，以构建混合源模型。GOD利用这些混合模型分别评估学生嵌入与教师编码器的匹配度，以及学生编码器与教师嵌入的匹配度。
tldr: 本文提出GOD框架，通过组件级嫁接蒸馏方法，分别评估学生嵌入和编码器与教师组件的匹配度，从而解耦并提升序列推荐的泛化能力。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes GOD, a component-level grafting distillation framework that separately evaluates student embeddings and encoders against teacher components to disentangle and improve generalization in sequential recommendation.
